title: kith-events: push delivery and reconnect tests
description:
What: Integration tests for the full EventSource push pipeline. Oracles from JMAP RFC 8620 spec and manual inspection.

Tests to implement:
1. test_push_delivery_new_message: Create make_channel(64); get Store with events_tx set; call message::insert; assert subscriber received StateChange{type_name:"Message", new_state matches store.messages().get_state()}. Oracle: RFC 8620 §7.1 state type names are capitalized object type names.
2. test_push_delivery_chat_update: call chat::update_last_message_at; assert Chat StateChange received.
3. test_push_no_emit_noop: call contact::set_blocked with unknown peer_user_id (no-op); assert no StateChange emitted (receiver.try_recv() returns Empty).
4. test_auth_peer_rejected: call events_handler with MockWhoIs returning a Peer identity; assert response status 403. Oracle: JMAP spec §7.3 says EventSource is owner-only.
5. test_types_filter: send Contact and Message StateChanges; subscribe with types=["Message"]; assert only Message events appear in SSE stream.
6. test_closeafter_state: subscribe with closeafter=state; send one StateChange; assert SSE stream ends after one event.
7. test_reconnect_replay: insert message (advances state), then call events_handler with Last-Event-ID set to state BEFORE insert; assert replay SSE event emitted for Message type before live stream starts.
8. test_lagged_receiver_skips: overflow broadcast channel buffer; assert stream continues (no panic, no 500); next real event is still received.

Oracle methodology:
- Expected SSE event data is JSON fragment hardcoded from RFC 8620 §7.1: {"changed":{"a-self":{"Message":"s-N"}}} where N is the integer returned by get_state()
- Auth oracle: independent MockWhoIs fixture that explicitly returns Role::Peer
- Never use code under test to derive expected values
